source_table: Fig 4D
notes: Text: 'whereas the short 15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer enhanced PF4 binding only at very high concentrations (at 320 ug/mL: 3.57-fold increase +/-1.1; Figure 4D)'. n=3. Graded 1 EXPLICITLY on the concentration-relative-to-clinical-exposure rule: the fold increase is large but is seen only at 320 ug/mL, roughly 500x the concentration at which the 57mer/77mer act and far above any plausible therapeutic aptamer plasma level. Only the anti-PF4/antigenicity axis is captured here; the aptamer's on-target antithrombin anticoagulant pharmacology is intended mechanism, not toxicity, and is deliberately excluded.

notes: Fig 5B-C legend: 'Except for the short 15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer, which induces platelet aggregation after 19.0 +/- 0.67 minutes and only in 66.6% of all donors, lag time and reactivity of platelets show only minor differences between the constructs.' source_table: Fig 5D
notes: Text: 'They reacted only very weakly with PF4/15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer complexes (at 40 mg/mL: mean OD: 0.431 +/- 0.064; Figure 5D)'. n=4. SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY: the Fig 5D legend describes this as 'no binding to complexes of PF4 and the 15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer (40 ug/mL, n = 4)', whereas the prose reports weak but measurable binding at OD 0.431 (above the 0.02-0.28 control-sera range, but at/below the ~0.6 dashed threshold line drawn in Fig 5D). Graded 1 on the prose value (weak reactivity, and only at the highest tested aptamer concentration); the legend reading would make it grade 0. Shortest and least structured of the four aptamers - lowest antigenicity, consistent with the length/structure model.

notes: THE MECHANISTIC ROW. Normal human bone marrow cells treated with 0, 0.9, 1.875, 3.75, 7.5 or 15 uM imetelstat; 'significantly inhibited the number of MK colony growth at >= 3.75 uM'. readout_value TBD because no colony counts or percentages are printed (Applicant Figure 1 is a bitmap). Exposure anchor computed from the review's own unit conversions: the document equates 750 ug/mL with ~150 uM (printed p48), giving ~5 ug per umol, so the popPK-predicted human Cmax of 89.2 ug/mL at the approved 7.1 mg/kg dose is ~18 uM - the 3.75 uM threshold is roughly 0.2x total human Cmax, i.e. BELOW therapeutic plasma concentration, not supra-clinical.
